M2.claim: Every adjacent strict-inversion swap lowers I by exactly 1 (exhaustive, n<=8 distinct keys)

M2b.claim: Same with duplicate keys (strict inversions, alphabet 3, n<=7)

M3.claim: Non-adjacent swap of an inverted pair lowers I by 1+2k (odd, can exceed 1); swapping a non-inverted pair raises I. So 'dI=-1 on every single swap' holds only for adjacent swaps
M3.source: Dietz Claim 2 verdict vs. Selection long-range swaps

M4.claim: I has no non-global local minimum under adjacent transpositions (n<=8)
M4.source: Dietz Conclusion 'permutations have no local minima'

M5.claim: [2a,2b,1c] swap first/last -> [1c,2b,2a]: equal keys reversed without being compared

M7.claim: Endpoint chance benchmark holds for EVERY sort whose permutation ignores labels (stable or not); a departure refutes label-independence of movement, not stability as such
M7.source: bears on Dietz 'critics predict flat 0.50' and Sweet's acceptance of it

M8.claim: Serotonin (z=+1) equilibrium ratio across -20 vs -60 mV is ~4.7

M9.claim: Scoreboard arithmetic reproduces 77.6, 65.7, 88.1; the superseded pillar mean is 81.68 (81.7) from exact cards, 81.6 only from rounded inputs with Thompson written as 96.0 instead of 96.1

M10.claim: 57.9% (7 Thompson modes) <= 86.2% (7-PC PCA) is required by Eckart-Young; '+13% to +48%' over 2.4% are ratios 6.4x-21x, so '15x' needs a stated base

M11.claim: Landauer kT ln 2 at 300 K ~ 2.87e-21 J per erased unbiased bit

M12.claim: A = H/N = (N - R)/N, so the chance benchmark is the Wald-Wolfowitz runs-test null: E[R] = 1 + 2bs/N
